page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

The underlying x86_64 Intel processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile and AMX_int8), which accelerate machine learning and cryptographic workloads. Cryptographic operations are further supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in database operations and image processing. It demonstrates strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, text processing, and Redis SET operations, which reached 71.84 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 4457.66 GB/sec, though large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. LLM inference speeds are strong for small and medium models, but text generation for large 70B models is average at 4.24 tokens per second.

Given its high compute-to-memory ratio and lack of bundled local storage, the n4-highcpu-64 offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is highly suited for database operations, software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated Intel vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 128 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier performance in database operations and image processing, alongside strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis operations. Small-block cached memory bandwidth is highly efficient, though large-block uncached memory performance is average. This instance is qualitatively cost-effective for high-throughput, CPU-intensive tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as database management, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale CPU-based LLM inference.
